g.text: (A3-2) and leaves (A3-3); AGV-4 enters (A4-3). Every link is an edge SCP keeps.

g.text: S[W22] = [A1-1, A2-2, A3-3, A4-4]. Between two

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: consecutive leavers of W22, someone must have entered

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: it (here A2-1, then A3-2). That entering move got an edge

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: from the previous leaver, and its own AGV's type-1 chain

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: leads to the next leaver. So A1-1 reaches A2-2 and A2-2

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: reaches A3-3, and one edge A3-3 → A4-3 is enough.

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: (b) Corner case: the latest candidate is the target's own AGV

g.text: A separate tiny plan on four places u, v, w, x: AGV-5 leaves v at t = 1; AGV-6 enters v (A6-1), leaves to w

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: (A6-2) and comes back (A6-3). For A6-3, S[v] = [A5-1, A6-2]: the search lands on A6-2, AGV-6 itself.

g.text: Why the latest candidate is enough (Theorem 3)

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Every move that leaves a place is ordered after every earlier move that left it, through the AGVs that entered in between. So a target only needs an edge from the most recent leaver;

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: edges from older leavers (red, added by CP) are implied.
